summary: The 2026 LLM landscape is dominated by a handful of frontier families—OpenAI's GPT, Google's Gemini, and Anthropic's Claude—which together capture the vast majority of consumer web traffic and enterprise API spend. Real-world developer adoption is increasingly shaped by cloud aggregator reach (AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, Google Vertex AI, Snowflake Cortex, IBM watsonx), where enterprises consume models through secure platforms rather than direct vendor APIs. Open-weight families like Meta's Llama, Alibaba's Qwen, and DeepSeek hold strong positions in self-hosted and HuggingFace download metrics even where direct API share is modest.

models.name: GPT-5.x (GPT-5 / GPT-5.2)
models.popularity_notes: ChatGPT held ~54-56% of worldwide generative-AI web traffic in 2026 and OpenAI models drive the plurality of API usage; available via Azure OpenAI Service across global enterprises.
strengths: Reliable function calling and structured output
models.best_for: General-purpose production applications requiring top-tier reasoning and broad ecosystem support

models.name: Gemini 2.5 Pro / 3.1 Pro
models.popularity_notes: Gemini's web visits grew ~450% YoY to 2.9B monthly visits (25-28% share) and it is natively distributed through Google Vertex AI to enterprise customers.
strengths: Native Vertex AI / Google Cloud integration
models.best_for: Long-document analysis, multimodal tasks, and Google Cloud-native deployments

models.name: Claude Opus 4.x / Claude 4.6
models.popularity_notes: Claude leads enterprise API usage at ~40% share (Menlo Ventures) and reached ~952M monthly web visits (+855% YoY); available through AWS Bedrock and Google Vertex AI.
strengths: Available on AWS Bedrock and Vertex AI
models.best_for: Enterprise coding, agentic systems, and safety-critical production workloads

models.name: Claude Sonnet 4.x
models.popularity_notes: The Sonnet tier is Anthropic's most-used model for high-volume developer workloads due to strong price/performance and broad Bedrock/Vertex aggregator availability.
models.best_for: High-volume production coding and agent workflows needing balanced cost and quality

models.name: Llama 4
models.popularity_notes: The leading open-weight family by HuggingFace downloads and self-hosted deployments; distributed across AWS Bedrock, Azure, Google Vertex AI, Snowflake Cortex, and IBM watsonx.
strengths: Broadest aggregator availability of any open model
models.best_for: Self-hosted and fine-tuned deployments where data control and cost matter

models.name: DeepSeek-V3.2
models.popularity_notes: Holds ~4% of chatbot web traffic and significant OpenRouter/HuggingFace volume thanks to very low cost and open weights, though usage normalized after its early-2025 spike.
strengths: Popular on API aggregators like OpenRouter
models.best_for: Cost-sensitive reasoning and coding workloads, especially self-hosted

models.name: Qwen3
models.popularity_notes: Adopted by over 90,000 enterprises and a top HuggingFace download leader; a dominant open-weight choice in Asia and increasingly available via cloud platforms.
models.best_for: Multilingual applications and self-hosted deployments, particularly in Asian markets

models.name: GPT-5 mini / GPT-4o mini
models.popularity_notes: The low-cost OpenAI tier drives enormous developer API call volume for high-throughput tasks and is available directly and via Azure OpenAI Service.
strengths: Very low cost at high volume
models.best_for: High-volume, latency-sensitive tasks like classification, extraction, and chat at scale

models.name: Gemini 2.5 Flash
models.popularity_notes: Google's fast, low-cost tier captures heavy developer volume for scaled workloads and ships through Vertex AI to enterprise customers.
models.best_for: High-throughput long-context and multimodal processing on Google Cloud

models.name: Grok-4
models.popularity_notes: Holds ~2.4% of chatbot web traffic (up YoY) with growing developer adoption driven by X integration and real-time data access.
models.best_for: Applications needing real-time data and up-to-date conversational responses

models.name: Mistral Large / Mistral Small
models.popularity_notes: A leading European model family with meaningful open-weight downloads and enterprise adoption via AWS Bedrock, Azure, and Vertex AI, clustering close to the #10 tier.
models.best_for: EU-based and data-sovereignty-focused deployments needing open-weight flexibility
